3.speaker: Narrator
3.text: Sordland One's flight from Holsord to Staalport took three hours but went very smoothly. We were about to touch down.

4.speaker: Narrator
4.text: Deivid left his seat and came over while Symon was enjoying his newspaper.

5.speaker: Deivid Wisci
5.text: “Looks like we are about to land, Mr. President.”

6.speaker: Narrator
6.text: I looked outside. I could see Heljiland, the island in between Valgsland and Agnolia.

7.speaker: Deivid Wisci
7.text: “So many conflicts over such a small piece of land. The island can barely sustain itself without outside help.”

8.speaker: Player
8.text: “I don't blame them. It is in a very strategic position.”

9.speaker: Player
9.text: “I know. I was just thinking the same thing.”

10.speaker: Player
10.text: “If I was in the shoes of the Agnolian Prime Minister, I would do anything to protect the motherland.”

11.speaker: Deivid Wisci
11.text: “Thousands of people died fighting for it. I wonder if it was worth it.”

12.speaker: Deivid Wisci
12.text: “Of course. But as I get older, I started to question more things.”

13.speaker: Deivid Wisci
13.text: “Certainly. If you have Heljiland, you are in control of the whole Valgos Channel.”

14.speaker: Deivid Wisci
14.text: “I suspect it will be one of the topics that Mr. Van Hoorten will bring up as a bargaining chip. We must be careful.”

15.speaker: Deivid Wisci
15.text: “Heljiland might be under the control of Agnolia, but the international community has yet to recognise it. For a good reason, too.”

16.speaker: Deivid Wisci
16.text: “Nobody wants to make an enemy of Valgsland. Especially because of the support of United Contana and the CSP.”

17.speaker: Player
17.text: “Me included. I wouldn't want do anything to injure our relationship with Valgsland.”

18.speaker: Player
18.text: “I don't care who we're up against. We will cross that bridge when we come to it.”

19.speaker: Symon Holl
19.text: “Aside from the point of Heljiland, we need to be careful with the additional requests.”

20.speaker: Deivid Wisci
20.text: “We should try to look at the bigger picture.”

21.speaker: Deivid Wisci
21.text: “I agree. We should try our best to stick to the middle ground.”

22.speaker: Narrator
22.text: Symon folded his newspaper, got up from his seat and sat right next to us.

23.speaker: Symon Holl
23.text: “According to the deal that was negotiated so far, they want to sell us their steel for a higher price and they are requesting easier access to our agricultural market.”

24.speaker: Symon Holl
24.text: “In return, they are promising cash flow and investments, especially in the Agnland region. It's not hard to guess why.”

25.speaker: Deivid Wisci
25.text: “During the initial negotiations, they brought up the topic of immigration many times.”

29.speaker: Deivid Wisci
29.text: “The fact that we have relaxed our immigration laws will help tremendously.”

30.speaker: Deivid Wisci
30.text: “Our job will be harder because of our new tightened immigration laws.”

31.speaker: Deivid Wisci
31.text: “Let's see if we can shake hands on it.”

32.speaker: Narrator
32.text: The pilot made an announcement that the descent had started. Deivid and Symon went back to their seats.

33.speaker: Narrator
33.text: I took another look outside the window. I could see Staalport, the capital city of Agnolia.

34.speaker: Narrator
34.text: The large dockyards of the city and the canals -- "Staal" in Agnolian -- appeared closer as our descent continued. Staalport was certainly a fitting name.

35.speaker: Narrator
35.text: A couple of minutes later, we finally touched down. The plane parked. I took a final look out the window. The welcoming ceremony from Agnolia was waiting along the red carpet outside.

36.speaker: Narrator
36.text: After the guards made their way out, I exited the plane.

39.speaker: Narrator
39.text: Prime Minister Van Hoorten was nowhere in sight. Instead, I was greeted by the Foreign Minister.

40.speaker: Narrator
40.text: After handshakes and a couple of photos, I moved to the car where Serge was waiting to drive me to the office of Prime Minister.

41.speaker: Serge Wolkner
41.text: “Good day, sir. I hope the flight was comfortable.”

45.speaker: Narrator
45.text: I got in the car and we made our way through the foreign streets. Our convoy was protected by Sordish and Agnolian guards in their vehicles.

46.speaker: Narrator
46.text: We got on the highway beside the port and saw dozens of dockyards and ships anchored. Some of the boats and machinery looked old.

47.speaker: Narrator
47.text: The city itself looked very grey and grim. The buildings had a touch of Rumburg's famous Monarkian architecture with a mixture of Sordish signature domes on the older ones.

48.speaker: Narrator
48.text: We were now on the main road to the office of the Prime Minister.

49.speaker: Serge Wolkner
49.text: “Looks like they are not too happy to see you, sir.”

50.speaker: Narrator
50.text: Serge pointed at the crowd that gathered on both sides of the street. It was a protest. They were shouting and yelling at our convoy. Some of them held signs written in Sordish: 'Go Home Rayne', 'We Don't Want Autocrats In Agnolia.'

51.speaker: Serge Wolkner
51.text: “You know... I never knew Agnolians were so ungrateful. Not everyone sees a great leader like you everyday.”

53.speaker: Player
53.text: “You are absolutely right, Serge. So ungrateful.”

54.speaker: Player
54.text: “There have been so many issues in Sordland. I don't know if I can call myself a great leader.”

55.speaker: Serge Wolkner
55.text: "I know what it is. They were always scared of Sordland's potential. And now they are afraid that a lion leads Sordland. They are afraid of you."

56.speaker: Serge Wolkner
56.text: “Sir, humility is important but not in this case. They were always scared of Sordland's potential. And now they are afraid that a lion leads Sordland. They are afraid of you.”

57.speaker: Serge Wolkner
57.text: “Not just that, but you are a man who is selfless enough to help your driver's children.”

65.speaker: Serge Wolkner
65.text: “He is fine, sir. A strong boy. Takes after his namesake for sure!”

66.speaker: Serge Wolkner
66.text: “I can attest to that myself. I am honored to be your driver. And very grateful.”

67.speaker: Serge Wolkner
67.text: “Very well, sir. I just want to say that I am honored to be your driver. And very grateful.”

70.speaker: Narrator
70.text: The car continued through the gates while the security vehicles went the other way. We finally came to a stop in front of the door.

71.speaker: Narrator
71.text: Serge left the car and opened the car door. I exited and began walking to the door where dozens of press and the Prime Minister were waiting for me.

72.speaker: Narrator
72.text: I saw the PM much more clearly as I neared the door. He was shorter than I thought.

73.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
73.text: “Mr. President. Welcome to Agnolia and to the beautiful city of Staalport.”

74.speaker: Player
74.text: “Thank you so much for the warm welcome. It is great to be here.”

77.speaker: Narrator
77.text: He reached out for a handshake. The press surrounding us had been waiting for this moment.

82.speaker: Narrator
82.text: He gestured to the entrance of the two-hundred-year old Parliament building.

83.speaker: Narrator
83.text: We entered and the press followed us inside.

84.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
84.text: “I would like to present you with a gift as a sign of friendship between our countries.”

85.speaker: Narrator
85.text: An assistant showed up immediately with a large glass case in her hands. It contained a single sheet of parchment inside.

86.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
86.text: “This here is one of the first treaties written between Sordland and Agnolia. May it mark the renewal of our friendship today as well!”

88.speaker: Player
88.text: “This is an amazing gift. Thank you.”

90.speaker: Narrator
90.text: Our photos were taken again. I gestured at one of my retainers who was holding our gift to the PM.

91.speaker: Player_Italic
91.text: Gift a Sordish-bred puppy despite Maartin's known fear of dogs.

92.speaker: Player_Italic
92.text: Gift one of the original copies of the first constitution of Sordland.

93.speaker: Player_Italic
93.text: Gift an ornamented ceremonial sword made with Sordish steel.

94.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
94.text: “Ah! An excellent copy. I have always wondered what one of the originals looked like. Thank you for this excellent gift.”

95.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
95.text: “Ah! An excellent specimen. This must be hundreds of years old. It looks like this is Sordish steel as well. Very fitting. Thank you.”

96.speaker: Narrator
96.text: Maartin stepped backwards when the puppy howled. He very uncomfortably held the dog in his hands and tried to smile at the reporters before putting the dog down on the floor.

98.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
98.text: “Let's go to my office. Follow me.”

99.speaker: Narrator
99.text: I followed him and we entered the office of the Prime Minister. With its minimalist wooden decor, the room was far more modest than I expected.

100.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
100.text: “Sheesh. I'm thankful to be done with the ceremonies.”

101.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
101.text: “Would you like a drink, Mr. Rayne?”

102.speaker: Player
102.text: “Are you not fond of these ceremonies?”

103.speaker: Player
103.text: “I was just about to say the same. I'm not fond of these either.”

104.speaker: Narrator
104.text: We sat down. He leaned back and made himself comfortable.

106.speaker: Narrator
106.text: He got up from his chair and moved over to the bar. There were many varieties of liquor.

111.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
111.text: “Ah, you're keeping it Sordish. A very good whiskey for sure.”

113.speaker: Narrator
113.text: He poured the drinks and gave mine to me before sitting down again.

114.speaker: Player
114.text: “What was with that protest outside? Can't you control them?”

115.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
115.text: “Lashing out at me before we even start discussing the trade deal? Please look at your own country first before indulging yourself with Agnolian matters, Mr. Rayne.”

118.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
118.text: “First of all, if we shake hands on it, this agreement is going to be extremely beneficial for both of us.”

119.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
119.text: “You should be able to solve your recession in no time with the investment and money flow coming from us. This is, as you know, on top of the reduced tariffs for trade between our countries.”

120.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
120.text: “Of course in return, as discussed between my people and your people before, you will allow us privileged access to your agricultural market.”

121.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
121.text: “First of all, I would like to say that I have been watching your recent immigration policy changes. I am glad that you have decided to keep it relaxed.”

125.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
125.text: “First of all, I would like to say that I have been watching your recent immigration policy changes. We have worries about the new and tighter immigration laws.”

126.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
126.text: “Immigrants are very important for beneficial economical development. We believe that very much in Agnolia.”

127.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
127.text: “Immigrants are very important for beneficial economical development. We believe that very much in Agnolia.”

128.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
128.text: “I would definitely prefer Sordland to be welcoming to Agnolian citizens and vice versa.”

129.speaker: Player
129.text: “Before I start caring about Agnolian citizens, I must care about my own people.”

131.speaker: Player
131.text: “Why don't you deal with the problems in your own country first?”

132.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
132.text: “Unfortunately, because we share a direct border, I can't simply ignore the problems of Sordland.”

133.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
133.text: “A valid point, but you are not giving me much incentive to work with.”

134.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
134.text: “It is reassuring to see Sordland move in a more modern direction.”

136.speaker: Player
136.text: “Are you implying we haven't been modern?”

137.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
137.text: “Well, certainly not under Tarquin Soll. What did you call him? Corporal Soll? General Soll?”

138.speaker: Player
138.text: “*Colonel* Soll and you will learn to respect him.”

139.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
139.text: “No need to get angry because of our differing opinions.”

140.speaker: Narrator
140.text: He took a sip from his vodka.

142.speaker: Player
142.text: “I see you did your homework. We think alike. Don't you worry. I will modernize the country.”

143.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
143.text: “Exactly. Now is the time of Anton Rayne.”

144.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
144.text: “That is...actually very good and refreshing to hear. I hope you can do it.”

148.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
148.text: “I know that you have declared a state of emergency. So early into your presidency, too. So, tell me. How is that going?”

149.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
149.text: “So tell me, Mr. Rayne. Is Sordland a reliable trading partner to Agnolia?”

150.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
150.text: “But it is precisely my business. I need to know if Sordland is a reliable trading partner.”

151.speaker: Player
151.text: “I had no choice but to deal with our issues in Sordland.”

153.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
153.text: “It is worrying that a state of emergency was declared right next to our borders.”

154.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
154.text: “Sometimes we leaders have to make tough choices. But you need to understand that I need trustworthy trading partners.”

155.speaker: Player
155.text: “It is going well. We are eliminating the threats one by one. Internal *and* external.”

156.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
156.text: “The reason I am asking these questions is because I need to know if Sordland is a reliable trading partner.”

157.speaker: Player
157.text: “Not if you keep acting like *you* have the upper hand.”

158.speaker: Player
158.text: “As long as Agnolia is a reliable trading partner.”

159.speaker: Player
159.text: “Of course, Mr. Van Hoorten. You can trust Sordland.”

161.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
161.text: “Then you see, we might have a problem.”

166.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
166.text: “It was a good move to start building that highway. Overall, this will positively affect our trade.”

168.speaker: Narrator
168.text: Van Hoorten leaned back further in contemplation.

170.speaker: Player
170.text: “Are you going to talk all day about past deeds or are we going to sign this deal?”

179.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
179.text: “You will be buying steel from us for a higher price, which is a small price to pay really. That is the deal.”

183.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
183.text: “I'm afraid with all your actions so far, I am not convinced that Sordland is the right partner for Agnolia.”

186.speaker: Player
186.text: “This is not a beneficial deal for Sordland.”

187.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
187.text: “You went through all this effort to come and say no to me?”

189.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
189.text: “I'm sorry that you've come all this way for this.”

193.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
193.text: “Before we dive into the paperwork for the trade deal, I want to offer you another possibility.”

194.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
194.text: “I would like to expand on our new partnership. We have regional forces like Rumburg that have been imposing danger on both of our countries. I am of the mind that we must unite. So...”

195.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
195.text: “By the powers bestowed upon me as the Prime Minister of Agnolia, I am offering a military alliance between Sordland and Agnolia.”

197.speaker: Player
197.text: “Sordland is not ready to go that far with Agnolia.”

199.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
199.text: “That is unfortunate. It would've been beneficial against the Rumburg threat. However, Agnolia can stand by itself against any threat just fine.”

200.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
200.text: “That is excellent to hear. Our ministers will go over the details later.”

201.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
201.text: “Now that we have gone this far and are willing to enter an alliance, there is another topic that I would like to bring up.”

202.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
202.text: “As you know, Heljiland has been long contested between Agnolia and Valgsland. Those warmongers want to take back the island.”

203.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
203.text: “You know how the international community does not recognise our rightful claim on the island. *Including Sordland*.”

204.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
204.text: “What better act to cement our alliance than announcing to the world that Sordland recognises Heljiland to be Agnolian territory?”

208.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
208.text: “It is a reasonable request, but I won't push too far on the matter. We have achieved enough for today.”

209.speaker: Deivid Wisci
209.text: “Precisely. Agnolian immigrants in our Agnland region make up a good chunk of the area's economy now.”

210.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
210.text: “I think they are a waste of time, but alas, that is one of our jobs.”

211.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
211.text: “It's one of the tougher parts of our job.”

212.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
212.text: “You are throwing many months of work down the drain. This is a mistake.”

213.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
213.text: “I took you for someone you were not, I suppose. But you are no different than your predecessors.”

217.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
217.text: “Congratulations, Mr. Rayne, for making all the right decisions today.”

218.speaker: Narrator
218.text: He stood up from his chair.

219.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
219.text: “We must continue the official program. As you know, we will pay a visit to our founder's grave for another ceremony. Afterwards, we will move on to the state dinner.”

221.speaker: Player
221.text: “Be careful with your words, Mr. Van Hoorten.”

222.speaker: Player
222.text: “You are in no position to judge me. I have made my decision.”

223.speaker: Player
223.text: “There is nothing else to talk about. We are done here.”

224.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
224.text: “I thought this could be the start of a new era, but apparently not.”

226.speaker: Player
226.text: “Did you bring me here to ridicule me?”

228.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
228.text: “Solve your own problems first before you threaten me, Mr. Rayne.”

230.speaker: Player
230.text: “I won't be joining. It's time we were on our way back home.”

232.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
232.text: “But this is customary. Every Sordish president before you has done this. This won't sit well with us. I must insist we follow the protocol.”

236.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
236.text: “This is outrageous. You are not giving confidence to the people of Agnolia right now.”

237.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
237.text: “But it is your decision, after all.”

238.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
238.text: “Very well. I will let them know that you are heading out.”

239.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
239.text: “See you later, Mr. President. We will be in touch.”

240.speaker: Narrator
240.text: I got up from my chair.

241.speaker: Player
241.text: “You are very welcome to come visit Sordland.”

246.speaker: Narrator
246.text: Outside, Serge was waiting for me. I got in the car and we started driving back to the airport.

247.speaker: Narrator
247.text: I briefed Symon and Deivid. The trip back was mostly silent.

248.speaker: Narrator
248.text: I couldn't help but let out a sigh of relief when we touched down in Holsord.

249.speaker: Narrator
249.text: As soon as we left the office, I briefed Symon and Deivid on the outcome of the meeting.

250.speaker: Narrator
250.text: The rest of our state trip was full of fake smiles, handshakes, incredibly long ceremonies and even longer meetings between our ministers and their counterparts.

251.speaker: Narrator
251.text: When we came to the end of the trip, the way back was mostly silent.

255.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
255.text: “We were willing at first, but the situation has changed. We do not have confidence in your state anymore.”

256.speaker: Narrator
256.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Turn01_InT_Investment_Highway"] == true) and (Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn04_RegionalInvestment_Agnland"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn04_RegionalInvestment_Agnland"] == true) == false)

258.speaker: Player
258.text: “I didn't do it for Agnolia. I did it for the people of Sordland.”

260.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
260.text: “Of course. Everything we do is for our people.”

265.speaker: Narrator
265.text: Serge pointed at the crowd that gathered on both sides of the street. It was a protest. They were shouting and yelling at our convoy. Some of them held signs written in Sordish: 'Sordland Must Pay Its Debts To Agnolia'

266.speaker: Player
266.text: “I wonder what propaganda their state is feeding them..."

267.speaker: Serge Wolkner
267.text: "They are afraid of you, sir. They are scared that Sordland will reach its potential. They don't want you to be seen as the great hero you are."

268.speaker: Player
268.text: “I'm sorry, but I can't agree to this."

269.speaker: Player
269.text: “I can't agree to the higher prices. We prefer to continue with the current steel deal.”

270.speaker: Player
270.text: “Agnolian steel isn't worth that much, Mr. Van Hoorten.”

271.speaker: Player
271.text: “I'm sorry but my answer is no.”

272.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
272.text: “Is that so? You'd rather import it from Rumburg then?”

273.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
273.text: “We believe that Sordland has been given an unfair advantage for too long because of the previous agreements. We can no longer accept this, Mr. Rayne.”

274.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
274.text: “Our people believe that we have long been overshadowed by Sordland. I am here to fix that. With a beneficial trade for both us, nonetheless.”

276.speaker: Player
276.text: “Then I will accept, Mr. Van Hoorten. We don't want to lose such an important partner as Agnolia.” [-1 Government Budget]

277.speaker: Player
277.text: “I'm sorry but my answer is no.”

278.speaker: Player
278.text: “Look, Mr. Van Hoorten. Let's discuss if lower prices are possible.”

279.speaker: Player
279.text: “No, but that does not change the fact that the prices are too high.”

280.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
280.text: “We don't want to lose our cooperation with Sordland. Maybe I can agree with the old prices. I will offer an alternative for the sake of our history together.”

281.speaker: Player
281.text: “I agree. Sordland will recognize the island.”

282.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
282.text: “Wouldn't it be fitting for Sordland to finally announce the recognition of Heljiland as Agnolian territory? If you do that, we'll have a deal.”

283.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
283.text: “You know how the international community does not recognise our rightful claim on the island. *Including Sordland*.”

284.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
284.text: “As you know, Heljiland has been long contested between Agnolia and Valgsland.”

286.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
286.text: “Sordland is rejecting a trade deal that rights the wrongs of the past, and doesn't recognize its partners' territories... Yet we are the ones asking for too much?”

294.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
294.text: “But there is another topic I would like to bring up.”

295.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
295.text: “As you know, Heljiland has been long contested between Agnolia and Valgsland. Those warmongers want to take back the island.”

296.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
296.text: “You know how the international community does not recognise our rightful claim on the island. *Including Sordland*.”

297.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
297.text: “Wouldn't it be fitting for Sordland to finally announce the recognition of Heljiland as Agnolian territory?”

298.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
298.text: “But I will still offer an alternative for the sake of our history together.”

299.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
299.text: “As you know, Heljiland has been long contested between Agnolia and Valgsland.”

300.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
300.text: “We can only agree to this deal if Sordland finally announces the recognition of Heljiland as Agnolian territory.”

301.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
301.text: “You know how the international community does not recognise our rightful claim on the island. *Including Sordland*.”

303.speaker: Player
303.text: “Fair enough. Sordland will recognise the island and Agnolia's other conditions.” [-1 Government Budget]

306.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
306.text: “And you will buy steel from us for a higher price that rights the wrongs of the past.”

307.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
307.text: “First, you will allow us privileged access to your agricultural market.”

318.speaker: Serge Wolkner
318.conditionsRaw: Variable["BaseGame.Country_Unrest"] > 0  and  (Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_EnT_LawEnforcement_Budget_Increase"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Autocrat_Path"] == true)

319.speaker: Serge Wolkner
319.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Country_Unrest"] > 0  and  (Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_EnT_LawEnforcement_Budget_Increase"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Autocrat_Path"] == true)) == false

377.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
377.text: “This here is one of the first treaties written between Sordland and Agnolia. Just like the one you prepared with Mr. Wisci before my term. May it mark the renewal of our friendship today as well!”

378.speaker: Maartin Van Hoorten
378.text: “Sordland is simply too volatile. Elected politicians are getting killed in your country left and right. Not to mention the subsequent protests in between...well...the left and right.”

379.speaker: Narrator
379.text: It was time to discuss the good news.
